title: The Picnic That Came to You
premise: At the foot of a sunny hill, Lila and Moss the donkey plan a picnic for Aunt Juniper, who cannot climb. Their small wagon can carry only two picnic bundles. Depending on what they know, what Juniper wants, and whose pride gets in the way, the picnic may become a hilltop feast, a rolling meadow party, or a brave little performance beside the road.
cast_and_props: Characters: Lila, an inventive child who wants Aunt Juniper to feel included; Tomas, her younger brother, who wants to reach the hilltop and ring the picnic bell; Moss, a proud donkey who wants to be treated as a guest rather than a cart. Aunt Juniper is represented as the invited guest and may be at the hill foot. Props: two-bundle wagon, picnic basket, blue quilt, brass bell, paper crown, jar of berry fizz. Shared setting: the hill path, its foot, and its grassy top. State slots include each character's location, wishes and beliefs; wagon capacity/load; ownership of props; invitation, agreement, picnic location, performance and guest delight.
kernels_and_interactions: 1. Observe/tell: Lila can discover or tell others that Juniper cannot climb, and Tomas can learn that Moss dislikes being loaded like a machine. These beliefs enable different requests and choices. 2. Transfer: children can hand the bell, crown, or basket to Moss or Juniper, changing who leads the celebration. 3. Move/carry: a bundle is loaded into the wagon only when capacity permits; Moss can pull it only after agreeing. 4. Negotiate: Moss may agree to pull, Tomas may agree to stay below, and Juniper may accept either a hilltop invitation or a foot-of-hill celebration. 5. Perform/share: ringing the bell, crowning Moss, or laying the quilt establishes concrete final outcomes and guest delight.
seed_parameters: Seed 3125356339 should initialize one of three physical/social conditions: (A) both bundles are already in the wagon and the bell is at the hilltop, so the children must choose what to leave behind; (B) Moss believes the plan is to haul everything while Tomas believes Juniper will climb, creating a mistaken-belief problem; (C) Juniper has arrived at the hill foot with a sore knee and privately wants a quiet celebration, while Tomas wants the daring hilltop picnic. Vary initial ownership of the bell and crown, Juniper's expressed preference, and whether Moss's agreement is known. Premise keys: wagon load, Juniper location/ability, Moss's belief about his role, Tomas's wish. Outcome keys: picnic location, Moss agreement/contentment, guest delight, performed celebration.
candidate_scenes: Use 16 candidates, selecting about 6–9. Shared scenes: Lila observes Juniper's climbing problem; Lila tells Tomas; Tomas asks Moss what he wants; Moss agrees to pull; the children load one bundle; they spread the blue quilt; final bell or crown scene. Distinct problem scenes: 'discover_empty_capacity' forces a choice between food and decorations; 'correct_tomas_belief' reveals Juniper is already below the hill; 'hear_juniper_preference' reveals she wants a quiet foot picnic; 'moss_refuses_cart_role' blocks hauling until the crown or bell is offered; 'invite_hilltop' succeeds only if Juniper can or wants to go; 'make_meadow_party' moves the quilt and basket to the foot; 'moss_leads_procession' lets Moss pull one bundle proudly; 'ring_bell_for_guest' performs the hilltop celebration; 'crown_moss' performs the foot-of-hill celebration; 'share_berry_fizz' marks guest delight. Reuse observation, negotiation, loading, quilt-spreading, and sharing across all paths, with guards on knowledge, capacity, ownership, location, and agreement. Mark only 'correct_tomas_belief' and 'moss_refuses_cart_role' pivotal.
constraints: Define every scalar slot before use; every key begins with an entity ID. Use 3–5 kernel families and at least one observe/tell action that enables a later choice. No abstract counters, branch-number routes, or unsupported knowledge. The inciting action must be an invitation, loading action, or observed problem before any response. Keep 12–22 candidates, 5–10 selected events, prune=True, and require goals to be physical/social facts. Catalog every candidate scene, including previews, with conditional prose. Do not claim Juniper climbed unless her location and ability support it. Do not make Moss haul both bundles when capacity forbids it.
different_endings: 1. Hilltop feast: Juniper reaches the top or accepts the invitation, the quilt is spread, and the brass bell rings; final image: the bell's tiny notes tumble down the hill toward empty picnic plates. 2. Meadow welcome: Juniper stays at the foot, the children bring one chosen bundle, and the quilt becomes a bright meadow table; final image: Moss wears the paper crown while berry fizz bubbles in his cup. 3. Proud donkey procession: Moss agrees to pull one bundle and leads a short celebration to Juniper; final image: he stops beside her with the bell tied to his harness, waiting for applause. Give each ending two warm voice variants, guarded by actual final location, agreement/contentment, performance, and guest-delight states.
